title: Run Planner
description: Describes one run: where it attacks, when it stops, and what it does in between. Every control says whether the bot has actually been shown working.

presets.title: Town Hall Smart Attack starting points
presets.description: Research-guided run settings for every current Home Village Town Hall. Choosing one loads its complete preset-owned settings, explicitly selects the Town Hall Hero loadout, and enables the bounded local Smart Attack policy. Recommended army names are guidance only; the bot does not silently replace your profile army.

items.description: Uses the active profile army, selects no Heroes, and spreads along every small-village side. The GiArch name is guidance; no army is silently retrained.

sections.title: Destination
sections.description: Picks the exact battle surface. This is stored as an exact surface rather than a general mode, so choosing Legend I cannot end up running the Legend III path.

settings.label: Battle surface
settings.summary: The exact screen the run attacks from.
settings.description: Regular and Ranked are separate surfaces with separate rules, and the three Legend tiers have different attack budgets. Picking the exact one keeps the bot from falling back to whatever the old coordinates happen to respond to.

options.label: Regular Battles
options.summary: Unlimited attacks, no Trophy risk.
options.description: Ordinary matchmaking. Attacks are unlimited and Trophies are not at stake, which makes this the surface to use while you are still confirming that a build behaves the way you expect.

options.label: Ranked Battles
options.summary: Attack count is reported by the client.
options.description: Tournament matchmaking with a limited number of attacks per tournament. The bot will not start until it has read how many attacks you actually have left, because the published limit is not your remaining count.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.
prerequisites: Remaining attacks visible on the Ranked screen

options.label: Revenge
options.summary: One attack per defence log entry.
options.description: Attacks a Shadow Base from your defence log. Each entry can be attacked once and the opportunity expires, so this surface is driven by what is in the log rather than by a repeating schedule.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.
prerequisites: An eligible entry in the defence log

options.label: Legend III
options.summary: Limited to 24 attacks per week.
options.description: The entry Legend tier, with a weekly attack budget. The budget shown in the catalog is the published maximum for the tier, not the attacks you have left this week.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.

options.label: Legend II
options.summary: Limited to 30 attacks per week.
options.description: The middle Legend tier, with a larger weekly attack budget than Legend III.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.

options.label: Legend I
options.summary: Limited to 8 attacks per league day.
options.description: The top Legend tier, budgeted per League Day rather than per week, so the remaining count resets on a different schedule from the lower tiers.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.

options.label: Builder Base Battles
options.summary: Attack count is reported by the client.
options.description: Builder Base matchmaking. Runs against the Builder Base economy and upgrade flow rather than the Home Village one, including the additional Builder.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no adapter for this battle surface; selecting it cannot start a run.

settings.label: Attack strategy
settings.summary: Which deployment routine runs once a base is found.
settings.description: Strategies come from the existing attack code. The CSV strategies are the inherited scripted deployments; the others depend on recognition that has not been re-confirmed yet.

options.label: Scripted (CSV)
options.summary: Runs a deployment script from the Strategies folder.
options.description: Uses the CSV deployment scripts that ship with the bot. This is the most predictable option because the deployment order is written down rather than decided from the base layout.
options.disabled_reason: The CSV actuator is wired, but a complete current-client deployment has not passed supervised review.
prerequisites: At least one CSV strategy present

options.label: Standard deployment
options.summary: The built-in side and line deployment routine.
options.description: A supervised run confirmed Standard could issue the trained-army and selected-Hero deployment, observe an empty troop bar, and return home. That single completion confirms the route and actuator, not strategy quality; it did not exercise planned ability or spell actions.

options.label: Smart Attack (research-guided)
options.summary: Concentrates the current army using a Town Hall-aware local policy.
options.description: The deterministic Town Hall policy is versioned in config/game/smart-attack-strategies.json and executed locally. One bounded supervised TH17 run verified three zoom gestures, 240 red-line points, deterministic BL-side selection, 23-to-zero troop deployment, four selected Hero phase commands, Rage 3-to-zero, one proven Freeze decrement, and an automatic one-battle stop. This verifies the mechanics on that run, not strategy quality or every Town Hall and army.
options.warning: Runtime-observed on one TH17 current-army battle; quality, other Town Halls, and other armies remain unverified.

options.label: Smart farm
options.summary: Targets collectors and storages based on the base layout.
options.description: Reads the base to choose where to drop, which needs current building recognition including the Town Hall 18 additions.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no Smart farm adapter.

options.label: Builder Base routine
options.summary: Deployment routine for Builder Base battles.
options.description: A Builder Base specific deployment. It is not implemented against the current Builder Base layout yet.
options.disabled_reason: Not implemented for the current Builder Base layout.

settings.label: Attack script
settings.summary: The exact bundled CSV deployment used for this run.
settings.description: A named script overrides both dead-base and live-base CSV selection in memory for one run, then the saved profile selection is restored. Choosing a file never changes the profile and never starts the bot.

options.label: Use profile selection
options.summary: Keeps the script already selected in the active profile.
options.description: Does not replace the active profile's script for this run. Use this with Standard deployment, or when the profile already names the exact CSV deployment you want.
options.disabled_reason: The profile selection is wired, but its resolved deployment has not completed supervised current-client proof.

sections.title: Heroes
sections.description: Chooses which Heroes the run treats as active. The Hero Hall holds six but only four can be active at once, so this is a selection rather than a fixed list.

settings.label: Active Heroes
settings.summary: Up to four Heroes from the six in the Hero Hall.
settings.description: Heroes below your Town Hall level are released automatically rather than left selected, so the run never plans around a Hero you cannot field. In current-trained-army mode the selected Heroes are deployed when their attack-bar slots are present, but the bot does not open Hero Hall or wait for Hero training.

options.label: Barbarian King
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 4. Movement: ground.
options.description: Ground Hero, and the first one you unlock. Available from Town Hall 4. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Hero Hall recognition has not been captured on the current client, so the bot cannot confirm which Heroes are actually in your active slots.

options.label: Archer Queen
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 8. Movement: ground.
options.description: Ranged ground Hero with high single-target damage. Available from Town Hall 8. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Hero Hall recognition has not been captured on the current client, so the bot cannot confirm which Heroes are actually in your active slots.

options.label: Minion Prince
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 9. Movement: air.
options.description: Air Hero, so terrain and ground defences affect it differently from the King or Queen. Available from Town Hall 9. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Hero Hall recognition has not been captured on the current client, so the bot cannot confirm which Heroes are actually in your active slots.

options.label: Grand Warden
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 11. Movement: mode-dependent.
options.description: Support Hero whose movement follows the mode you set, ground or air. Available from Town Hall 11. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Hero Hall recognition has not been captured on the current client, so the bot cannot confirm which Heroes are actually in your active slots.

options.label: Royal Champion
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 13. Movement: ground.
options.description: Ground Hero that targets defences first. Available from Town Hall 13. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Hero Hall recognition has not been captured on the current client, so the bot cannot confirm which Heroes are actually in your active slots.

options.label: Dragon Duke
options.summary: Unlocks at Town Hall 15. Movement: air.
options.description: Air Hero added in the February 2026 update. Available from Town Hall 15. The Hero Hall holds six Heroes but only 4 can be active at once, so selecting this Hero may require freeing a slot.
options.disabled_reason: Dragon Duke is not present in the inherited five-Hero deployment engine.

sections.title: Emulator
sections.description: Chooses which Android emulator the run drives and which instance of it, since a single machine commonly has several instances configured.

settings.label: Emulator
settings.summary: Which emulator the bot attaches to.
settings.description: Leave this on automatic unless you run more than one emulator. MEmu, LDPlayer 9 and MuMu have native adapters, but each still needs a dated controlled run on its current release before support can be promoted.

options.label: Detect automatically
options.summary: Uses whichever supported emulator is already running.
options.description: Looks for a running, supported emulator and attaches to it. This is the right choice for a single-instance setup.

options.label: BlueStacks 5
options.summary: The inherited BlueStacks 5 backend.
options.description: Verified on BlueStacks 5.22.252.1008/Pie64 through exact window binding, ADB readiness, current-client game readiness, and bounded Start/Stop smoke tests. This does not claim a completed attack.

options.label: MEmu
options.summary: Inherited exact-instance MEmu backend.
options.description: Discovers MEmu VM instances, reads their ADB host and port from VM information, uses the emulator-owned ADB when available, and selects background capture from the active renderer. The architecture was compared with the MIT MyBotPy MEmu implementation, but no code or templates were imported and no local MEmu runtime test is available on this machine.
options.disabled_reason: Adapter is statically checked but has not passed a current MEmu 9.5.3 hardware smoke test.
options.warning: Do not assume that ADB connection alone proves capture, clicks, drag, zoom, or recovery.

options.label: Nox
options.summary: The inherited Nox backend.
options.description: Carried over from the upstream bot and not re-tested against current Nox builds.
options.disabled_reason: Not re-tested against current Nox builds.

options.label: LDPlayer 9
options.summary: New adapter with multi-instance ADB addressing.
options.description: Discovers installed instances and addresses them on port 5554 plus twice the instance index, which is how LDPlayer 9 assigns ADB ports to multiple instances.
options.disabled_reason: Adapter is written but has not been run against real hardware.
options.warning: Expect to report problems from the first few runs.

options.label: MuMu Player 12
options.summary: New adapter reading per-instance ADB ports.
options.description: Reads each instance's ADB endpoint from the emulator rather than assuming a fixed port, and adapts background capture to the active renderer.
options.disabled_reason: Adapter is written but has not been run against real hardware.
options.warning: Expect to report problems from the first few runs.

settings.label: Instance
settings.summary: Which emulator instance to attach to.
settings.description: Choose the exact named instance shown by the attached emulator. BlueStacks 5 requires an explicit instance so capture, input, and the native controller dock cannot target different accounts.

sections.title: Army
sections.description: How the army gets built between battles. Training no longer has wait times, so this is about what to build rather than how long to wait for it.

settings.label: Army source
settings.summary: Where the troop composition comes from.
settings.description: Army Recipes replaced the old training queue, so a saved recipe is now the natural unit of army setup rather than a per-troop count.

options.label: Saved Army Recipe
options.summary: Use one of the recipes saved in game.
options.description: Picks a saved Army Recipe and trains it. This is how the current client expects armies to be set up, and it survives balance changes better than a fixed list.
options.disabled_reason: Army Recipe screen recognition has not been captured.

options.label: Cookbook entry
options.summary: Use an entry from the Cookbook tab.
options.description: The Cookbook holds shared and suggested armies. Selecting from it needs the third army tab to be recognised.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no Cookbook army adapter.

options.label: Fixed troop list
options.summary: The inherited per-troop composition.
options.description: Trains a fixed list of troops the way the older bot did. Kept because it does not depend on recipe recognition, but it ignores anything the game has changed since.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no fixed-list army-source adapter.

settings.label: Recipe name
settings.summary: Which saved recipe to train.
settings.description: The exact recipe name as it appears in game. Left blank, the run uses whichever recipe is already selected rather than switching.
settings.native_fixed_reason: Named Army Recipe selection is not wired; the run can only use the active profile army.

settings.label: Manage training
settings.summary: Allow this run to change the training queue.
settings.description: Leave this off for one battle with the army already trained in game. The bot still checks whether that army is ready, but it will not boost Super Troops, inspect or edit Quick Train, remove troops, queue troops or spells, or build siege machines. Turn it on only when the active profile's army composition is current and this run should retrain.
prerequisites: Current training, Quick Train, spell, and siege screen recognition
settings.disabled_reason: The inherited training routine exists, but its current-client screen flow has not been captured and supervised end to end.
settings.warning: Use only as a supervised diagnostic until a full train-wait-attack cycle is recorded.

settings.label: Wait for a full army
settings.summary: Do not attack with a partly trained army.
settings.description: Holds the run until the army is complete. Worth leaving on: attacking short-handed wastes the attack more often than the wait costs.

settings.label: Train spells
settings.summary: Brew spells as well as troops.
settings.description: Includes the spell portion of the army. Turn off to save Elixir on cheap farming runs.

settings.label: Build sieges
settings.summary: Build a siege machine each run.
settings.description: Builds the siege machine the recipe calls for. Only useful where a Clan Castle troop matters.

sections.title: Base search
sections.description: What counts as a base worth attacking. Every filter that is set has to pass before the run commits to an attack; a zero means the filter is off.

settings.label: Minimum Gold
settings.summary: Skip bases offering less Gold than this.
settings.description: Reads available loot before committing. Set to zero to attack regardless of Gold on offer.

settings.label: Minimum Elixir
settings.summary: Skip bases offering less Elixir than this.
settings.description: Same idea as the Gold filter, applied to Elixir. Zero turns it off.

settings.label: Min Dark Elixir
settings.summary: Skip bases offering less Dark Elixir than this.
settings.description: Dark Elixir loot is an order of magnitude smaller than Gold or Elixir, so this wants a correspondingly smaller number.

settings.label: Give up after
settings.summary: Stop searching once this long has passed.
settings.description: A long search costs a Gold search fee each skip. This caps how long the run will hunt before taking what it can find. Zero means no cap.
settings.native_fixed_reason: The inherited search loop has no safe elapsed-time exit, so this value must remain zero.

settings.label: Town Hall filter
settings.summary: Which defender Town Hall levels to accept.
settings.description: Filtering by defender Town Hall needs the bot to read the Town Hall on the search screen, which changed with Town Hall 18.

options.label: Any Town Hall
options.summary: Accept whatever matchmaking offers.
options.description: No filtering. The safest setting while search-screen recognition is unconfirmed, because it does not depend on reading the defender's Town Hall at all.

options.label: Lower than mine
options.summary: Only bases below your Town Hall level.
options.description: Prefers weaker defenders. Requires reading the defender Town Hall reliably.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract currently accepts only Any Town Hall.

options.label: Same or lower
options.summary: Bases at or below your Town Hall level.
options.description: A looser version of the above, trading some safety for a shorter search.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract currently accepts only Any Town Hall.

sections.title: Pacing
sections.description: How hard the run drives the emulator. Every value here trades throughput for fewer misread screens, and the defaults are the point where that trade stops paying.

settings.label: Gap between actions
settings.summary: Shortest wait between two taps. Zero drives the emulator as fast as it answers.
settings.description: The bot can issue taps faster than an emulator redraws, and an action sent into a screen that has not finished changing lands on whatever was underneath it. This sets a floor on the gap between one action and the next. The wait is only taken when the previous action finished more recently than this, so a slow step costs nothing extra.

settings.label: Screen settle wait
settings.summary: How long to let a screen finish changing before reading it.
settings.description: Applies after anything that starts an animation: opening a menu, dismissing a dialog, returning from a battle. Reading pixels while the frame is still moving is the largest single source of misidentified screens, and waiting here costs far less than acting on a wrong one.

settings.label: Retries per action
settings.summary: Reserved for handlers that can prove a tap changed nothing.
settings.description: Generic retries are unsafe without a visual-change observer: repeating a successful destructive tap can do the wrong thing twice. Keep this at zero until a screen-specific handler can prove the first action was dropped; Start rejects nonzero values instead of guessing.
settings.native_fixed_reason: Generic retries have no visual-change observer in the native engine and must remain zero.

settings.label: Rest after
settings.summary: Pause the run once it has been going this long. Zero never pauses.
settings.description: Hours of unbroken emulator load is where thermal throttling and memory growth start showing up as misread screens. This schedules a pause so the machine gets a gap. The run resumes by itself afterwards; nothing is closed and no progress is lost.

settings.label: Rest for
settings.summary: How long each scheduled pause lasts. Ignored when rests are off.
settings.description: The run stops issuing actions for this long and then picks up where it left off. Time spent resting still counts against the run duration limit, so a long rest on a short run can end it before the next battle.

sections.title: Stop conditions
sections.description: Decides when the run ends. Any condition that is set can stop the run; leaving a value at zero turns that condition off.

settings.label: Run for
settings.summary: Stop after this many minutes. Zero means no time limit.
settings.description: Measured from the moment the run starts, not from when the first battle begins, so time spent waiting for troops counts against it.

settings.label: Battle limit
settings.summary: Stop after this many battles. Zero means no limit.
settings.description: Counts every battle the run starts, won or lost. On a surface with a limited attack budget the remaining count still applies on top of this.

settings.label: Stop at Star Bonus
settings.summary: Stop once the Star Bonus is earned.
settings.description: Ends the run as soon as the Star Bonus is complete, which is the usual stopping point for a daily farming session.

settings.label: Failure limit
settings.summary: Stop after this many consecutive problems.
settings.description: A failure is a battle that could not be completed, not a battle that was lost. Keep this low while testing an unverified surface so a broken run stops quickly.

sections.title: Resource targets
sections.description: Stops the run once a resource total has been collected. Each target is counted across the run, and zero turns the target off.

settings.label: Gold
settings.summary: Stop once this much Gold has been collected.
settings.description: Counts Gold taken during the run, not the Gold currently in your storages.

settings.label: Elixir
settings.summary: Stop once this much Elixir has been collected.
settings.description: Counts Elixir taken during the run, not the Elixir currently in your storages.

settings.label: Dark Elixir
settings.summary: Stop once this much Dark Elixir has been collected.
settings.description: Counts Dark Elixir taken during the run. Dark Elixir loot is much smaller than Gold or Elixir, so this target wants a correspondingly smaller number.

sections.title: Donating
sections.description: Answering clan mate requests between battles. Donation happens through clan chat, whose navigation changed when Global Chat arrived.

settings.label: Donate
settings.summary: Whether and how to answer requests.
settings.description: Donating earns Clan XP and keeps a clan happy, but it costs training resources and time between attacks.

options.label: Do not donate
options.summary: Ignore requests entirely.
options.description: Skips the clan chat step completely, which is also the fastest option between battles and the one least dependent on chat recognition.

options.label: Only matching requests
options.summary: Donate when the request text matches.
options.description: Reads the request and donates only what was asked for. Depends on reading clan chat, which moved when Global Chat was added.
options.disabled_reason: Clan chat recognition has not been captured since Global Chat.

options.label: Donate anything
options.summary: Fill any request with whatever is available.
options.description: Donates without matching the request. Fast, and reliably annoys clan mates who asked for something specific.
options.disabled_reason: Clan chat recognition has not been captured since Global Chat.
options.warning: Expect complaints if your clan cares what it receives.

settings.label: Protect attack army
settings.summary: Protect troops the run needs to attack with.
settings.description: Refuses any donation that would leave the army short. Worth keeping on, since donating the army away and then attacking with what is left wastes the attack.
settings.native_fixed_reason: The native planner always protects the attack army; allowing donations to consume it is not wired.

settings.label: Donation limit
settings.summary: Stop donating after this many per run. Zero means no limit.
settings.description: Caps how much time and Elixir a single run puts into donating.
settings.native_fixed_reason: Per-run donation accounting is not wired, so the limit must remain zero.

settings.label: Request when empty
settings.summary: Ask the clan for Clan Castle troops.
settings.description: Posts a request when the Clan Castle is empty, so a defending or attacking castle troop is available.
prerequisites: Current Clan Castle request dialog recognition
settings.disabled_reason: The request path is inherited but has no current-client supervised receipt.
settings.warning: A diagnostic run may post a real clan request.

sections.title: Events and lab
sections.description: The recurring things worth doing between attacks: Clan Games challenges and keeping the laboratory busy.

settings.label: Play Clan Games
settings.summary: Pick up and complete Clan Games challenges.
settings.description: Clan Games run on a schedule and reward magic items. Automating them means reading the challenge list and tracking points, neither of which has been re-confirmed.
prerequisites: Current Clan Games challenge list and progress recognition
settings.disabled_reason: Clan Games logic is inherited but has not been replayed on the current client.
settings.warning: A diagnostic run can accept or abandon a real challenge.

settings.label: Stop at points
settings.summary: Stop once this many Clan Games points are earned.
settings.description: Clan Games caps individual scoring, and going past the cap earns nothing. Set this to your clan's agreed limit. Zero means play until the event ends.
settings.native_fixed_reason: Clan Games point accounting is not wired, so this cap must remain zero.

settings.label: Laboratory
settings.summary: What to research when the lab is free.
settings.description: Keeping the laboratory busy is most of long-term progress. Choosing what it researches means reading upgrade costs and levels off the lab screen.

options.label: Leave it alone
options.summary: Do not start research.
options.description: The run ignores the laboratory. Right setting while lab recognition is unconfirmed.

options.label: Cheapest available
options.summary: Always start the cheapest research.
options.description: Keeps the lab permanently busy at the lowest cost. Needs the lab screen read accurately, including the Town Hall 18 additions.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract currently accepts only Laboratory off.

options.label: Follow a priority list
options.summary: Work down a configured order.
options.description: Researches in the order you specify, skipping anything unaffordable. Needs both lab recognition and a stored priority list.
options.disabled_reason: Priority lists are not implemented yet.

settings.label: Collect collectors
settings.summary: Empty mines and collectors each pass.
settings.description: Tapping collectors is low risk and adds up. It is skipped automatically when storages are already full, so it costs nothing to leave on.
settings.disabled_reason: Collector tapping exists in the inherited engine but lacks a current-client fixture and run receipt.
settings.warning: Use a supervised diagnostic until collector and full-storage handling are observed.

sections.title: Between battles
sections.description: What the run does with the resources it collects, and which accounts it rotates through.

settings.label: Upgrades
settings.summary: What the bot spends resources on between battles.
settings.description: Upgrade handling reads menus and costs from the client. Anything beyond walls needs current recognition of the upgrade screens, which has not been re-confirmed.

options.label: Nothing
options.summary: Collect resources and leave them alone.
options.description: The run does not spend anything. This is the right setting while you are confirming that a surface works at all.

options.label: Walls only
options.summary: Spend surplus on wall upgrades.
options.description: Puts spare resources into walls, which is the least risky upgrade because it does not occupy a Builder.
options.disabled_reason: Wall levels have not been re-confirmed for the current client.

options.label: Suggested upgrades
options.summary: Follow the in-game suggested upgrade list.
options.description: Uses the game's own suggestions, which requires reading the upgrade menu as it currently appears.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract has no suggested-upgrade adapter.

options.label: Everything
options.summary: Walls, buildings, laboratory, and Heroes.
options.description: The full upgrade routine across every category. It depends on the six-Hero layout and the Town Hall 18 building set.
options.disabled_reason: Not implemented against the current upgrade and Hero screens.

settings.label: Account queue
settings.summary: Local bot profiles to rotate through, in order.
settings.description: References bot profiles stored on this machine. No credentials, tokens, or Supercell ID details are kept here; the queue only records which local profile to switch to next.
settings.native_fixed_reason: Planner-driven account rotation has no native adapter; the current inspected account is pinned for the run.
settings.empty_state: No profiles queued. Stays on this profile.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.description: Getting told when something happens, so a run does not need watching. These are bot features rather than game ones, so they do not depend on client recognition.

settings.label: On run stop
settings.summary: Send a message whenever a run ends.
settings.description: Fires on every stop, including a clean finish, so a silent bot means it is still going.

settings.label: On errors
settings.summary: Send a message when the run hits a problem.
settings.description: Worth turning on before any diagnostic run, since an unverified surface is exactly the case where you want to hear about a failure quickly.

settings.label: Send to
settings.summary: Where notifications go.
settings.description: Uses the credentials already stored in the bot's own settings. Nothing is stored in the run plan.

options.label: Bot log only
options.summary: Write to the log and nowhere else.
options.description: No external service involved. The message lands in the log window and the JSONL event stream, which is enough when you are at the machine.

options.label: Telegram
options.summary: Send through the inherited Telegram integration.
options.description: Uses the Telegram bot token configured in the bot's own settings. Carried over from upstream and not re-tested against the current Telegram API.
options.disabled_reason: The native execution contract currently accepts only Bot log notifications.
prerequisites: Telegram token configured in bot settings

options.label: Windows notification
options.summary: Raise a desktop notification.
options.description: A local desktop notification. Only useful if you are at the machine, in which case the log usually tells you more.
options.disabled_reason: Not implemented.

sections.title: Diagnostics
sections.description: Controls whether the run is allowed to attempt work that has not been demonstrated on the current client, so that its behaviour can actually be observed.

settings.label: Allow unverified
settings.summary: Run surfaces with no capture yet.
settings.description: A surface that refuses to start cannot be debugged, so this lets the run proceed anyway. It changes nothing about what the bot has actually been shown to do: the session, its snapshot, and every log line stay marked unverified, and that mark cannot be cleared for the rest of the run.

settings.label: Diagnostic note
settings.summary: Who is watching this run, recorded with the results.
settings.description: Required before an unverified surface will start. It is written into the session so a log read later makes clear the run was being observed rather than left unattended.
settings.empty_state: Required before an unverified surface will start.
